meta.title: PrivaMesh - Private Encrypted Messenger
meta.description: Private, end-to-end encrypted messenger for iPhone, Android and Windows. No phone number, no email, no account - your keys and chats never leave your device.

hero.title: The {scramble} messenger that knows nothing about you
hero.lead: Private messaging with no phone number and no account database. Messages are end-to-end encrypted on your device and delivered to one-time addresses over a public decentralized transport. PrivaMesh is built to minimise metadata - not to pretend it does not exist.
hero.phoneAlt: PrivaMesh private messenger onboarding on iPhone - privacy by default, end-to-end encrypted

noServers.title: No servers - concretely
noServers.lead: Most "private" messengers still run servers that see who you talk to. PrivaMesh has none. Here is exactly where every piece of your data lives.

lifecycle.title: One message, three steps
lifecycle.lead: Send → Transport → Receive. No middle box, no inbox on someone else's computer.

steps.label: Send
steps.body: Your message is padded to a fixed size and sealed with AES-256-GCM under a fresh Double Ratchet key - on your device, before it ever leaves.

steps.label: Transport
steps.body: The encrypted blob travels over a public, decentralized transport, addressed to a one-time address. No account server ever holds it.

steps.label: Receive
steps.body: Your device retrieves and decrypts it locally with keys only you hold, then advances the ratchet. Only your device can read it.

metadata.title: Hide who. Hide when. Hide how.
metadata.lead: Encryption hides the message. PrivaMesh also hides the metadata - the who, when and how that a server would otherwise see.

cards.title: One-time addresses
cards.body: Every message is delivered to a fresh one-time address, so an observer cannot reconstruct who talks to whom. The social graph stays hidden.

cards.title: Cover traffic
cards.body: Decoy messages blend with real ones so an observer cannot tell when you actually send. Timing analysis gets nothing to work with.

cards.title: Fixed-size padding
cards.body: Every message is padded to a fixed size before it is sealed, so its length leaks nothing about the content inside.

crypto.title: End-to-end encryption, done properly
crypto.lead: PrivaMesh uses the same battle-tested primitives that secure the best encrypted messengers, adapted for a serverless world. Every message gets a fresh key, so a compromised key can't unlock your past or future conversations.
rows: Curve25519 handshake establishes a shared secret without a trusted key server.
HKDF + HMAC-SHA256 rotate keys every message for forward secrecy and post-compromise security.
Authenticated encryption seals each payload, padded to a fixed size to hide length.

faq.a: Yes. There is no PrivaMesh account server, relay, or message database. Encrypted messages travel over a public, decentralized transport, so there is nothing central to breach, subpoena, log, or shut down.

PrivaMesh uses an X3DH handshake over Curve25519 to establish keys, then a Double Ratchet (HKDF and HMAC-SHA256) that gives every message a new key. Payloads are sealed with AES-256-GCM and padded to a fixed size. You get forward secrecy and post-compromise security by default.

faq.q: Can I use PrivaMesh without a phone number or email?
faq.a: Yes. There is no phone number and no email. Your account is an account phrase that maps to encryption keys stored in the iOS Keychain - device-only and protected by Face ID or Touch ID.
None on any server, because there is no server. Delivery uses one-time addresses to hide the social graph, cover traffic hides when you send, and fixed-size padding hides message length.

faq.q: What happens if I lose my phone?
faq.a: Restore your account phrase on a new device to recover your identity. By design your chat history is not recovered - forward secrecy means old message keys are deleted, so nobody, including you, can decrypt past messages from the phrase alone.

cta.title: Stop trusting companies with your conversations
cta.lead: PrivaMesh replaces the company with math and the server with a public, decentralized transport. Your keys, your device, your words.
